title: Late Breaking Results: Scalable GPU-Friendly Parallelization for Sweep-Based Maze Routing
problem: GPU-accelerated maze routing algorithms struggle with limited GPU memory resources on large-scale VLSI designs; sweep-based methods generate excessive kernel launching overhead.
motivation: Global routing is a critical VLSI design stage; modern large-scale designs exceed GPU memory capacity, requiring memory-efficient parallelization strategies.
method: The technique bundles multiple electrical connections (nets) into a single routing pass (sweep) instead of routing them separately, which reduces GPU memory usage and the cost of repeatedly launching GPU operations. When a path gets blocked, the algorithm selectively recalculates only the problematic segment (edge-level rip-up-and-reroute) rather than starting over, preserving successful routes and speeding up the solution.
key_novelty: This technique is the first to route multiple electrical connections (nets) simultaneously within a single computational pass (sweep) rather than using multiple passes, reducing GPU memory consumption and computational overhead.
contributions: Sweep-sharing mechanism for simultaneous routing of multiple nets in single pass
Edge-level rip-up-and-reroute for selective re-routing of overflowed segments
Significant memory efficiency and runtime improvements on latest ISPD-24 benchmarks
primary_theme: Sweep-sharing for scalable GPU maze routing
